Question: The Fibonacci sequence \(1,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(5,\) \(8,\) \(13,\) \(21,\) \(\ldots\) starts with two \(1\)s, and each term afterwards is the sum of its two predecessors. Which one of the ten digits is the last to appear in the units position of a number in the Fibonacci sequence?
Solution:
Only the units digits of the preceding two terms are needed to find the next units digit. Higher places contribute whole tens, which do not change the units digit. Thus we add the preceding two units digits and keep only the units digit of their sum.

Let \(d_n\) be the units digit of the \(n\)th Fibonacci number. Starting with \(d_1=d_2=1\), this rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_1,\ldots,d_7&=1,1,2,3,5,8,3,\\
d_8,\ldots,d_{14}&=1,4,5,9,4,3,7,\\
d_{15},\ldots,d_{21}&=0,7,7,4,1,5,6.
\end{aligned}
\]
The first 20 entries contain each of \(0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9\), but no \(6\). The next entry is \(6\), so the last digit to appear is \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
